meta.title: Practice manager at a multi-provider outpatient clinic
meta.industry: Healthcare, outpatient clinic with eight providers
meta.blurb: Runs the front office, schedules and staff for a busy clinic. This role carries planted traps.
traps: No pattern fit: covering the front desk at lunch is hands-on work no catalog pattern fits.
Not enough detail: the facts sheet says nothing about how insurance payments are reconciled.
Hours over the week: the cards add up to more than the stated 40 hours.
Back-to-back meetings: three meeting cards in a row on most days.

opportunities.quote: I call insurers and check portals, then log status in my spreadsheet
opportunities.why: You spend time chasing insurers for updates on open requests and logging who has responded in a spreadsheet.
opportunities.firstStep: Move one recurring request into a form or workflow that sends reminders by itself.
opportunities.failureMode: People ignore automated reminders that arrive too often.

opportunities.why: You book and move appointments by phone with back-and-forth calls because patients have no online booking option.
opportunities.firstStep: Publish a booking page with your open hours and send it instead of proposing times.
opportunities.failureMode: Booking pages fill focus time unless protected blocks are set first.

habits.name: Gaps after back-to-back meetings
habits.firstStep: Set meetings you own to end five minutes early by default.
habits.failureMode: Other people's meetings still run to the hour.

noFit.taskName: Cover the front desk at lunch

thin.taskName: Weekly KPI report for the owners

rules.name: Task is in the task map
Quoted evidence appears word for word in the visitor's answers
Pattern is in the catalog and every required signal was recorded
Tool is listed on the pattern, with a working link checked within the limit
Hours figures are the ones code computed
A working-habit suggestion carries no hours unless the catalog supplies a share

transcript.question: For "Rebuild provider schedules", what triggers a rebuild, and who receives the finished schedule?
transcript.answer: Provider call-outs or added sessions trigger it; I rebuild the schedule by hand and send it to staff.

transcript.question: How many times a week do you rebuild provider schedules in "Rebuild provider schedules"?
transcript.answer: Whenever a provider calls out or adds a session, so probably 3-5 times a week.

transcript.question: About how many prior authorizations do you chase in "Chase prior authorizations" each week?
transcript.answer: About 20 open requests at a time, so roughly 10-25 I chase each week.

transcript.question: For "Chase prior authorizations", where do the requests come from, and where does the result go?
transcript.answer: Requests come from my open list of about 20 prior authorizations; I call insurers and check portals, then log status in my spreadsheet.

transcript.question: About how many patient calls do you handle each day in "Scheduling calls with patients"?
transcript.answer: About 25 calls a day to book and move appointments, since we have no online booking.

transcript.question: For "Scheduling calls with patients", who calls in, and where do the booked appointments get recorded?
options: Inbound calls; booked in EHR scheduler
Inbound calls; booked in paper book
Outbound reminder calls; booked in EHR
Mix of both; booked in EHR scheduler
transcript.answer: Mix of both; booked in EHR scheduler. About 25 calls a day to book and move appointments, and there's no online booking.
